plugin_description: Turns exteraGram into a CLI/TUI environment: a real shell, plugin and client control, and tooling for plugin authors.
open_console_desc: The terminal; .cli also works in any chat
diag_item_desc: Check which execution backends this device allows
appearance_note: The console follows your Telegram theme by default
auto_setup_desc: Unpack it and measure this device on first run, so apk and the rest work straight away
tools_item_desc: What is installed into Alpine on first run
tools_ask_message: Alpine comes with almost nothing. These are fetched from its own repositories and live in the container.
tools_look_desc: a fetch, a monitor, and things that are simply nice to watch
tools_pytools_desc: published on PyPI rather than in Alpine, so they need Python first
tools_utils_desc: git, an editor, and the archivers a shell is unusable without
tools_python_desc: python3 with pip, and uv to install anything else
tools_java_desc: what jadx and every Android tool needs
tools_javac_desc: javac, and the modules with it
mounts_item_desc: Which of the four paths a guest opens
data_item_desc: The container, the measurements, and how to delete them
mount_root_desc: The rootfs — where the programs live
mount_patch_desc: The client's own code, taken apart, under /patch
mounts_note: One has to stay on. With Alpine off the shell opens in the next one and its programs still run.
mounts_changed: Reopen the console to see the change
data_note: It lives outside the plugin's own folder so that updating the plugin does not throw away a container you have set up.
wipe_rootfs_desc: Alpine and everything installed into it
wipe_rootfs_question: Alpine and everything installed into it. It is unpacked again the next time the plugin loads.
wipe_all_desc: Removing the plugin leaves this behind; this is how it goes
wipe_all_question: The Linux container, every measurement taken of this device, and the shell history. The plugin's settings are kept.
advanced_item_desc: Entry points, the terminal renderer, logging
renderer_note: The compatible one is drawn with ordinary views. The fast one is newer and less proven.
debug_logs_desc: Log routine activity, not just failures
export_item_desc: Pack it into one file and send it somewhere safe
export_nothing: There is no container to export
export_question: Packs Alpine and everything installed into it into one file, then opens the share sheet so you can send it wherever you like — a chat with yourself works well.
keys_item_desc: The extra keys under the terminal — escape, tab, the arrows — arranged how you like
keys_hint: Tap a key to change it, + to add one.
keys_saved: Reopen the console to see the change
keys_ctrl: the next key is a control combination
keys_alt: meta, for a keyboard that has one
